words.ex: She gave a heartfelt thank you to her teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她向老师真诚地表达了感谢。
words.en: If you describe something such as a feeling or emotion as heartfelt, you mean that it is genuine and strongly felt.

words.tr: adj. 不可比拟的；无比的；无与伦比的；不能比较的；
words.ex: Her singing is incomparable.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌唱是无可比拟的。
words.en: If you describe something as incomparable, you mean that it is so good or great that nothing else can be compared to it.

words.ex: The weather was agreeable for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气令人愉悦，适合散步。
words.en: Pleasant and easy to like; willing to agree to something

words.tr: v. 组成；创作；“compose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The team is composed of five players.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队由五名队员组成。
words.en: If someone is composed, they are calm and able to control their feelings.

words.ex: The price of the phone is prohibitive for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了。
words.en: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that it prevents people from buying it or doing it.

words.ex: Her performance was phenomenal.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现非常非凡。
words.en: If you describe something as phenomenal, you think it is extremely good or impressive.

words.ex: His incisive comment solved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他一针见血的评论迅速解决了问题。
words.en: An incisive remark, question, or piece of writing is very clear and direct, and shows that the person understands something very well.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.tr: phrase. 看不见；在视野以外
words.ex: The keys are out of sight under the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙在沙发下面，看不见了。
words.en: If something is out of sight, it is too far away to be seen.

words.tr: v. 躺在…上面；把（婴儿）覆闷致死
words.ex: The sand overlie the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 沙子覆盖在岩石上面。
words.en: To lie over or upon something else; to cover.

words.tr: v. 插上电源；堵塞；宣传
words.ex: He plugged in the lamp and the room was filled with light.
words.ex_cn: v. 他插上了台灯，房间立刻充满了光亮。
words.en: To plug something means to connect it to an electrical supply, to block a hole or passage, or to promote or publicize something.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.tr: adj. 急剧的；引人注目的；戏剧（性）的；
words.ex: There was a dramatic increase in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度急剧上升。
words.en: If something is dramatic, it happens or changes suddenly and noticeably.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.tr: phrase. 缺乏的；没有的（通常与 'of' 连用，表示完全缺少某种特质或事物）
words.ex: The room was devoid of furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.tr: phrase. 结束；告终；意外到达
words.ex: He didn't plan to stay, but he ended up sleeping there.
words.ex_cn: 他本没打算留下，但最后在那里睡了。
words.en: If you end up in a particular place or situation, you are in that place or situation after a series of events, even though you did not originally intend to be.

words.tr: adj. 暴露的；无遮蔽的；易受攻击（或批评）的； v. 暴露；“expose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The baby's skin is exposed to the sun.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的皮肤暴露在阳光下。
words.en: If a place is exposed, it has no natural protection against bad weather or enemies, for example because it has no trees or is on very high ground.

words.ex: The rocket uses chemical propulsion to fly into space.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用化学推进力飞入太空。
words.en: Propulsion is the force that moves something forward, especially in vehicles like cars, planes, or spacecraft.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.tr: v. 扩大；扩张；更充分地阐述；“expand”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The company expanded its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司扩大了业务到其他国家。
words.en: If something expands or is expanded, it becomes larger.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.tr: adj. 随后的；后来的；接踵而至的； v. “ensue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ensuing meeting was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 随后的会议被取消了。
words.en: Following immediately after something else.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.ex: The medicine helps inhibit pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制疼痛。
words.en: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

words.tr: adj. 模糊的；不确定的；无限期的
words.ex: He gave an indefinite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不确定的答案。
words.en: If you describe something as indefinite, you mean that it has not been decided or defined clearly, or that it has no clear limit or end.

words.tr: v. （使）留痕迹；做标记；评分；“mark”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 明显的；显著的；有记号的；
words.ex: The storm marked the old tree with deep scratches.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在那棵老树上留下了深深的划痕。
words.en: A marked change or difference is very obvious and easily noticed.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.tr: adj. 倾斜的；有坡度的； v. “slope”的现在分词；
words.ex: The sloping roof lets rainwater run off easily.
words.ex_cn: 倾斜的屋顶让雨水容易流走。
words.en: Something that is sloping has a surface or edge that is at an angle, so that one end is higher than the other.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.tr: n. 设施；特色功能；特定场所；资质；
words.ex: The school has a new sports facility.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个新的体育设施。
words.en: A facility is a place, building, or service that is designed for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 悬浮；暂停；“suspend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The particles are suspended in water.
words.ex_cn: 这些颗粒悬浮在水中。
words.en: If something is suspended, it is hanging from somewhere or is not moving or active for a period of time.

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr: adj. 无可置辩的；无异议的；
words.ex: He is the undisputed champion of the tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他是这场比赛无可置辩的冠军。
words.en: If you describe a fact or opinion as undisputed, you mean that it is accepted as true or correct by everyone.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.ex: The company wants diversification to reduce risk.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望通过多元化来降低风险。
words.en: Diversification is the act of making something more diverse or varied, especially in business contexts where it refers to expanding into new markets or products.

words.ex: The new software vastly improves speed.
words.ex_cn: 新软件极大地提高了速度。
words.en: To a very great extent or degree.

words.tr: phrase. 逐渐习惯于；变得适应
words.ex: He grow accustomed to the cold weather after living in Canada for a year.
words.ex_cn: 在加拿大住了一年后，他逐渐习惯了寒冷的天气。
words.en: To gradually become familiar with something and accept it as normal or usual.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.ex: He got high scores in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中得了高分。
words.en: The number of points, goals, runs, etc., achieved in a game or by a team or an individual.

words.tr: phrase. 对…的痴迷；对…的执念；对…的过度关注
words.ex: He has an obsession with video games.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏着迷。
words.en: An obsession with something is a state in which you think about it all the time and find it hard to think about anything else.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.ex: The ball is a perfect sphere.
words.ex_cn: 这个球是一个完美的球体。
words.en: A sphere is a perfectly round three-dimensional shape, like a ball. It can also refer to a particular area of interest, activity, or knowledge.

words.tr: v. 传播；“diffuse”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The scent diffused through the room.
words.ex_cn: 香味弥漫了整个房间。
words.en: Spread over a wide area or between a large number of people.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: He will flee from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 他会从着火的房子里逃走。
words.en: If you flee from something or someone, you leave them quickly because you are afraid of them or because you do not want to be involved with them.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.ex: He copes with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To cope with a problem or task means to deal with it successfully.

words.ex: The stock market shows daily fluctuation.
words.ex_cn: 股票市场每天都有波动。
words.en: A fluctuation is a change in something, especially in a continuous process such as temperature, prices, or levels of activity.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.ex: The storm caused a disruption in the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴扰乱了火车服务。
words.en: Disruption is a situation in which something is prevented from continuing in its usual way because of problems or difficulties.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.ex: The volcano spewed hot magma into the air.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出了炽热的岩浆。
words.en: Magma is molten rock that is found beneath the surface of the Earth, and which may erupt from a volcano as lava.

words.ex: He left home prior to sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 他在日出前离开了家。
words.en: Before a particular time or event.

words.ex: The desert is inhospitable and has no water.
words.ex_cn: 这个沙漠不适合居住，也没有水。
words.en: If you describe a place as inhospitable, you mean that it is difficult to live or stay there because there is no shelter or the weather is bad. If you describe a person or their behaviour as inhospitable, you mean that they do not make people welcome.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.ex: The cat ran down the alley.
words.ex_cn: 猫跑进了小巷。
words.en: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings or other structures.

words.tr: phrase. 胡乱地； 随便地
words.ex: He picked a number at random.
words.ex_cn: 他随机选了一个数字。
words.en: If you choose people or things at random, you do not use any particular method, so they all have an equal chance of being chosen.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: His status in the company is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里的地位很高。
words.en: The status of someone or something is their position or situation according to the law or according to other people's opinions.

words.ex: The bird evolved from a small dinosaur.
words.ex_cn: 这种鸟由一种小型恐龙演变而来。
words.en: If something evolves or you evolve it, it gradually develops over a period of time into something different and usually more advanced.

words.ex: He likes coffee, whereas she prefers tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡，然而她更喜欢茶。
words.en: You use whereas to introduce a comment which contrasts with what is said in the main clause.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.ex: He made his decision after long deliberation.
words.ex_cn: 他在深思熟虑后做出了决定。
words.en: Deliberation is the long and careful consideration of a subject.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.tr:
n. 核；核心；重点；
adj. 核心的；
words.ex: The core of the apple is not edible.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的核心不能吃。
words.en: The central or most important part of something.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.tr:
n. 拥护者；信徒
adj. 黏附…的
words.ex: He is an adherent of the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他是这项新政策的拥护者。
words.en: An adherent is someone who supports a particular party, person, or set of ideas.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.tr: adj. 同时发生的；同步的；
words.ex: The two events happened synchronous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.tr: v. 恳求；辩护；答辩；以…为理由
words.ex: He pleaded for help when he was lost.
words.ex_cn: 当他迷路时，他恳求帮助。
words.en: If you plead with someone to do something, you ask them in an intense, emotional way to do it.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.tr:
n. 流体；流质；
adj. 流动的；
words.ex: Water is a common fluid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的流体。
words.en: A fluid is a substance that can flow and change its shape easily, such as a liquid or a gas.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: He was cautious when crossing the busy street.
words.ex_cn: 他过繁忙的街道时很小心。
words.en: If you are cautious, you are careful and avoid taking risks.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He opted to stay home instead of going out.
words.ex_cn: 他选择待在家里而不是出去。
words.en: If you opt for something, or opt to do something, you choose it or decide to do it in preference to anything else.

words.tr: v. 求爱；求婚；寻求支持
words.ex: He tried to woo her with flowers and chocolates.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和巧克力追求她。
words.en: If you woo someone, you try to persuade them to marry you or to have a relationship with you, or you try to gain their support or favor.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.ex: He averred that he was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他断言自己是无辜的。
words.en: To state or assert to be the case.

words.tr: v. 承认；公开宣称声明
words.ex: He avows his love for her.
words.ex_cn: 他坦承自己对她的爱。
words.en: If you avow something, you declare it or admit it openly.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；欠缺的；微小的；
words.ex: There is scant evidence to support the claim.
words.ex_cn: 支持这一说法的证据不足。
words.en: If you describe something as scant, you mean that there is not enough of it or that it is not as much as it should be.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.ex: His answer was apt for the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答对这个问题很恰当。
words.en: If someone is apt to do something, they often do it and so it is likely that they will do it again.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.tr: adj. 未固定牢的；宽松的；
words.ex: The loose screw fell off the table.
words.ex_cn: 那个松动的螺丝从桌子上掉了下来。
words.en: Not firmly or tightly fixed in place; detached or able to be detached.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.tr:
n. 漏洞；泄露；
v. 漏；泄露；
words.ex: The leak in the roof caused water to drip inside.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的漏洞导致水滴进屋里。
words.en: If a container or pipe leaks, or if it leaks a substance such as liquid or gas, the substance comes out of it accidentally because there is a hole or crack in it.

words.ex: The stone skimmed over the water.
words.ex_cn: 石头掠过水面。
words.en: To remove a substance from the surface of a liquid, or to read or consider something quickly in order to understand the main points, without studying it in detail.

words.tr:
n. 残疾；障碍；阻碍；不利
v. 妨碍；使不利
words.ex: He has a physical handicap but still runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有身体残疾，但仍然每天跑步。
words.en: A handicap is a condition that markedly restricts a person's ability to function physically, mentally, or socially.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: There was a surge in sales during the holiday season.
words.ex_cn: 假期期间销量激增。
words.en: If something surges, it increases suddenly and greatly, after having been steady or only small in size or amount.

words.tr: n. 支柱；中坚；中流砥柱
words.ex: His support has been the mainstay of the project.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持一直是这个项目的支柱。
words.en: If you describe something as the mainstay of a particular thing, you mean that it is the most basic part of it.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.ex: He is wanting a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一辆新自行车。
words.en: If something is wanting, it is lacking or not good enough in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The integration of technology and education improves learning.
words.ex_cn: 技术与教育的结合改善了学习。
words.en: The act or process of combining or adding parts to make a unified whole.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.ex: He acted on impulse and bought the car.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动买了那辆车。
words.en: An impulse is a sudden strong desire to do something without thinking about the consequences.

words.tr: 短语动词. 以…为特征；具有…的特点
words.ex: The city is characterized by narrow streets and old buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市以狭窄的街道和古老的建筑为特征。
words.en: To be characterized by something means to have it as a typical or noticeable feature.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.ex: It is worthwhile to learn a new language.
words.ex_cn: 学习一门新语言是值得的。
words.en: If something is worthwhile, it is enjoyable or useful enough to make the effort or money spent on it seem reasonable.

words.tr: v. 发现；找到；建立；认为；“find”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He found a strange stone on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上发现了一块奇怪的石头。
words.en: To establish or set up (an organization, institution, or place) on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.tr: adj. 可觉察的；很可观的
words.ex: There is an appreciable difference in his grades.
words.ex_cn: 他的成绩有明显的差异。
words.en: If something is appreciable, it is large enough to be noticed or considered important.

words.ex: The validity of the test results is important.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果的有效性很重要。
words.en: The quality of being logically or factually sound; soundness or cogency.

words.ex: He worked hard and prospered in business.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，在商业上取得了成功。
words.en: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.ex: Hard work makes success possible.
words.ex_cn: 努力使成功成为可能。
words.en: Enable something to happen.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.tr: n. 礼貌得体；适宜的举止
words.ex: He maintained decorum during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持了得体的行为。
words.en: Decorum is behavior that is controlled, calm, and polite, especially in formal situations.

words.ex: He signed his name with a clear signature.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的签名签了名字。
words.en: A signature is a person's name written in a distinctive way as a form of identification in authorizing a document or letter.

words.ex: The country is facing an economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正面临经济危机。
words.en: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.ex: He propose to go to the park after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提议午饭后去公园。
words.en: If you propose something, you suggest it as a plan or course of action.

words.tr: adj. 陷入困境的；受到限制的； v. 设圈套；陷入（困境）；“trap”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The hikers were trapped in the snowstorm.
words.ex_cn: 这些徒步者被困在暴风雪中。
words.en: If you feel trapped, you are in a situation that you cannot easily get out of.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: They jointly own the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们共同拥有这所房子。
words.en: If two or more people do something jointly, they do it together or in cooperation with each other.

words.ex: This portable charger works well on trips.
words.ex_cn: 这个便携式充电器在旅行时很好用。
words.en: Capable of being carried or moved about with ease.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: My teacher is tolerant of different opinions.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师对不同的观点很宽容。
words.en: If you describe someone as tolerant, you approve of the fact that they allow other people to say and do as they like, even if they do not agree with or like it.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.ex: The drawback of this phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature of something that makes it less useful or desirable than it could be.

words.ex: Tom and Jerry scored 80 and 90 points, respectively.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆和杰里分别得了80分和90分。
words.en: Respectively is used to indicate that the items in a list correspond to the items in another list in the same order.

words.ex: No wonder he is tired, he worked all night.
words.ex_cn: 难怪他累了，他整晚都在工作。
words.en: It is not surprising that something is the case.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: The manager oversees the team's daily work.
words.ex_cn: 经理监督团队的日常工作。
words.en: To oversee means to watch and direct a piece of work, the people doing it, or the way it is done in order to ensure that it is done correctly.

words.ex: His decisive action saved the team.
words.ex_cn: 他果断的行动拯救了团队。
words.en: If a fact, action, or event is decisive, it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.

words.ex: The two countries formed an alliance to fight the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成联盟以对抗敌人。
words.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

words.ex: The company announced redundancy due to low profits.
words.ex_cn: 公司因利润低下宣布裁员。
words.en: Redundancy refers to the state of being not or no longer needed or useful; the inclusion of extra components which are not strictly necessary to functioning, in case of failure in other components; or the dismissal of employees from work for being no longer necessary.

words.ex: I can detect a change in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 我能察觉到她情绪的变化。
words.en: To detect something means to find it or discover it, often using special equipment or methods.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr:
adj. 复杂的；
n. 综合楼（群）；
words.ex: The instructions are too complex for children.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明对孩子来说太复杂了。
words.en: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.ex: The weather is a determinant of whether we go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 天气是我们是否去远足的决定因素。
words.en: A determinant is a factor which decisively affects the nature or outcome of something.

words.tr: phrase. 继续；坚持；进行；开展
words.ex: He will carry on working after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后会继续工作。
words.en: If you carry on, you continue doing something.

words.ex: There is a correlation between exercise and good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼与健康之间存在相关性。
words.en: A correlation between things is a connection or link between them.

words.tr: adj. 易腐烂的；易坏的；易毁灭的
words.ex: Milk is a perishable food.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶是一种易腐食品。
words.en: Likely to decay or go bad quickly.

words.tr: adj. 边远的；偏远的；远离市镇的
words.ex: The outlying village has no bus service.
words.ex_cn: 这个偏远的村庄没有公交车服务。
words.en: Situated far from a center or main area.

words.tr: adj. 没有希望的；无前途的；不乐观的
words.ex: The weather looks unpromising for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气看起来不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something as unpromising, you think that it is unlikely to be successful or produce anything good in the future.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.ex: He ruled out the wrong answer on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中划去了错误的答案。
words.en: To decide that something is not possible or not worth considering.

words.ex: The number 5 corresponds to the letter E.
words.ex_cn: 数字5对应字母E。
words.en: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one is a cause or a result of the other.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: It is advantageous to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 早起是有利的。
words.en: If something is advantageous to you, it is likely to benefit you.

words.tr:
n. 毛孔；小孔
v. 细看；钻研；凝视
words.ex: Sweat comes out through the pores of the skin.
words.ex_cn: 汗水通过皮肤上的毛孔排出。
words.en: A pore is a tiny opening in a surface that allows liquids or gases to pass through. As a verb, to pore means to read or study something very carefully.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.tr: 短语. 表示对某事的失望或终结，常译为“别提…了”或“…到此为止”
words.ex: So much for our plans to go hiking this weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们的周末徒步计划到此为止。
words.en: used to indicate that something has not happened or been successful as expected, often expressing disappointment or irony

words.ex: The project was a monumental task.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是一项巨大的任务。
words.en: If you describe something as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, or that it is of great importance or significance.

words.ex: There is a five-minute interval between the two classes.
words.ex_cn: 两节课之间有五分钟的间隔。
words.en: An interval is a period of time between two events or dates.

words.tr:
n. 燃料；燃油；
v. 加剧；
words.ex: The rocket uses fuel 627 for propulsion.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用627号燃料推进。
words.en: Fuel is a substance such as coal, gas, or oil that is burned to provide heat or power.

words.ex: It rained all day, hence the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use hence to indicate that the statement you are about to make is a consequence of what you have just said.

words.tr: adj. 可辩解的；可证明为正当的；有理的
words.ex: His action was justifiable because he protected his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为是合理的，因为他保护了他的朋友。
words.en: If something is justifiable, there is a good reason for it.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.tr: v. 声称；“allege”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 所谓的；
words.ex: He alleged that the witness lied.
words.ex_cn: 他声称证人说了谎。
words.en: An alleged fact has been stated but has not been proved.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.ex: The police tried to subdue the angry man.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图制服那个愤怒的人。
words.en: To subdue someone or something means to bring them under control by using force or persuasion.

words.ex: Traffic congestion caused delays on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 交通堵塞导致了高速公路的延误。
words.en: Congestion refers to the state of being overcrowded, especially with traffic or people, or the condition of being blocked or clogged.

words.ex: The instructions were straightforward and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单，容易遵循。
words.en: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: The police found a clue at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了一条线索。
words.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps to solve a problem or mystery.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.ex: In essence, he is a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 本质上，他是一个善良的人。
words.en: You use in essence to emphasize that you are talking about the most important or central aspect of an idea, situation, or event.

words.ex: He is a renowned scientist.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有名的科学家。
words.en: Known or talked about by many people; famous.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.ex: The teacher will inspect our homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会检查我们的作业。
words.en: If you inspect something, you look at it very carefully, usually in order to find out something about it.

words.ex: The argument was pointless.
words.ex_cn: 这个争论毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe something as pointless, you are emphasizing that it has no purpose or is not worth doing.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.ex: The weather was unfavorable for the picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气对野餐不利。
words.en: If conditions or circumstances are unfavorable, they make it difficult for something to happen or exist.

words.ex: He wants to pursue his dream of becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他想追求成为作家的梦想。
words.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it.

words.tr: adj. 可比较的；比得上的；类似的；
words.ex: The prices of these two phones are comparable.
words.ex_cn: 这两部手机的价格是可比较的。
words.en: Something that is comparable to something else is similar in size, amount, or quality.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.tr: adj. 偏远的；隔离的；孤独的； v. 使隔离；“isolate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The village is isolated, far from any city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄很偏远，远离任何城市。
words.en: If something is isolated, it is far away from other places, buildings, or people.

words.ex: They have mutual respect for each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此相互尊重。
words.en: Mutual is used to describe a situation, feeling, or action that is experienced, felt, or done by each of two or more parties towards the other or others.

words.tr: v. 结盟；“ally”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: Two countries allied to fight the common enemy.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家结盟以对抗共同的敌人。
words.en: Allied means joined by or relating to members of an alliance.

words.ex: The book is a compilation of his best essays.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是他最佳文章的汇编物。
words.en: A compilation is a collection of different items, such as songs, pieces of writing, or data, that have been gathered together in one place or for one purpose.

words.tr: v. 使四下散开；散播；“disperse”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 分散的；散布的；
words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd with loudspeakers.
words.ex_cn: 警察用扩音器把人群驱散了。
words.en: If a group of people disperse or are dispersed, they go away in different directions.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: He adduce evidence to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他提出证据来证明自己的观点。
words.en: To cite as evidence or proof; to bring forward in argument or as proof.

words.tr:
prep. 除…以外；除非
v. 闩（门等）；阻碍；“bar”的现在分词
words.ex: Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the project will be completed on time.
words.ex_cn: 除非发生意外情况，否则项目将按时完成。
words.en: Unless there is something that prevents it from happening, barring is used to indicate that something will happen.

words.ex: He solely depends on his bike to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他只靠自行车去上班。
words.en: If something is solely the case, it is the only thing that is the case.

words.ex: He went for a walk regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去散步了。
words.en: Without taking into account; without being affected by.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.tr:
n. 化合物；
adj. 复合的；混合的；
words.ex: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水是由氢和氧组成的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.tr: adj. 易接近的；可使用的；简单易懂的；可进入的；
words.ex: The park is accessible by bus.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园乘公交车可达。
words.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach.

words.tr:
adj. 典范的；典型的；
n. 文学经典；名著；优秀的典范；
words.ex: This movie is a classic comedy.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部典范的喜剧。
words.en: A classic is something that is judged to be of the highest quality and outstanding of its kind.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: v. 围绕； adj. 有环的；圈出（ring 的过去分词）；
words.ex: The moon was ringed by a halo of light.
words.ex_cn: 月亮被一圈光晕围绕。
words.en: Having or wearing a ring or rings.

words.tr: adj. 贴邻的；毗连的； v. “adjoin”的现在分词；
words.ex: The two houses are adjoining.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子是贴邻的。
words.en: Adjoining is used to describe something that is next to or joined with something else.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.tr: vt. 调整；使有规则；对进行微调
words.ex: The engineer fine-tuned the engine to improve its performance.
words.ex_cn: 工程师对发动机进行了微调以提高其性能。
words.en: To make small adjustments to something in order to improve its performance or to make it more precise.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: He cleaned the room thoroughly.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底地打扫了房间。
words.en: In a thorough manner; completely and carefully.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.tr:
n. 功能；职责；
v. 起作用；
words.ex: The function of this button is to turn on the light.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮的功能是打开灯。
words.en: A function is the purpose that something is designed to have or the job that someone is employed to do. It can also refer to a mathematical relationship or a social event.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.ex: The new policy substantially improved the results.
words.ex_cn: 新政策实质上改善了结果。
words.en: To a great extent or degree; considerably.

words.ex: The music heightens the feeling of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 音乐加深了悲伤的感觉。
words.en: If something heightens a feeling or if the feeling heightens, the feeling increases in degree or intensity.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He is an intermediate student in English.
words.ex_cn: 他是英语的中级学生。
words.en: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

words.ex: I suspect it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我猜想明天会下雨。
words.en: If you suspect someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you believe that they have done it, although you have no proof.

words.tr:
adj. 迅速的；敏捷的；快的；
n. 雨燕；
words.ex: The swift runner won the race.
words.ex_cn: 这位迅速的跑步者赢得了比赛。
words.en: moving or capable of moving at great speed, or happening within a very short time; fast.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.ex: She was immensely happy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她赢得奖品后极大地开心。
words.en: To an extremely great extent or degree.

words.ex: The lion showed ferocity when it hunted.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在捕猎时表现出凶猛。
words.en: Ferocity refers to the state or quality of being ferocious, which means savagely fierce, cruel, or violent.

words.tr: phrase. 与……不一致；与……有分歧；与……争吵
words.ex: He is at odds with his brother over money.
words.ex_cn: 他因为钱的问题和他弟弟意见不合。
words.en: To be in disagreement or conflict with someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 狭窄的； v. “cramp”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The tiny room was cramped and hard to move in.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间很狭窄，很难活动。
words.en: If a place is cramped, it is not big enough for the people or things in it, so that it is difficult to move around or to use things properly.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 恰当的例子；典型的例子
words.ex: The recent scandal is a case in point of how corruption can destroy a company.
words.ex_cn: 最近的丑闻是腐败如何摧毁公司的典型例子。
words.en: A case in point is an example that illustrates or supports a general statement or argument.

words.ex: The school decided to adopt a new teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 学校决定采纳一种新的教学方法。
words.en: To adopt means to take up or start to use or follow (an idea, method, or course of action). It can also mean to legally take another's child and bring it up as one's own.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.ex: There is ample food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有足够的食物。
words.en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The soldier shoot at the target.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向目标射击。
words.en: To shoot means to fire a bullet from a gun or to take a photograph. It can also refer to the act of a plant sprouting or a player attempting to score in sports by sending the ball or puck towards the goal.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；性冷淡的（女子）
words.ex: The water is frigid in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的水很冰冷。
words.en: Frigid means extremely cold in temperature or lacking warmth or enthusiasm.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.ex: He wrote the book for posterity.
words.ex_cn: 他写这本书是为了留给后人。
words.en: All future generations of people.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.tr:
v. 小步疾走；急赶
n. 快跑声；疾走
words.ex: The mouse scurried under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠迅速跑到了桌子底下。
words.en: If people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: n. 标准；尺度；准则；“criterion”的复数；
words.ex: The main criteria for selection are skill and experience.
words.ex_cn: 选择的主要标准是技能和经验。
words.en: A criterion is a standard or principle by which something is judged or decided.

words.tr:
v. 补偿；赔偿；报酬
n. 报偿；回礼；赔偿
words.ex: The company recompense the worker for the lost time.
words.ex_cn: 公司补偿了工人损失的时间。
words.en: If you are given something, usually money, in recompense, you are given it as a reward or because you have suffered.

words.ex: The kidneys excrete waste from the body.
words.ex_cn: 肾脏将废物排出体外。
words.en: If someone excretes waste matter from their body, they get rid of it in faeces, urine, or sweat.

words.tr: adj. 分散的；散落的； v. 散布；分散；“scatter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The books were scattered on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 书散落在地板上。
words.en: If something is scattered, it is spread out or distributed over a wide area in an irregular way.

words.ex: We need to quantify the results of the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要量化实验的结果。
words.en: If you try to quantify something, you try to calculate how much of it there is.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.tr: 短语. 一瞥；稍微看到或了解到某事物
words.ex: She caught a glimpse of the Eiffel Tower as the plane flew by.
words.ex_cn: 当飞机飞过时，她瞥见了埃菲尔铁塔。
words.en: A brief or partial view of something.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: The report attests to his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告证明了他的努力。
words.en: To provide or serve as clear evidence of.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: The chair is stationary and does not move.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是固定的，不会移动。
words.en: not moving or not intended to be moved

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
words.en: A motif is a design or pattern that is used in a piece of art or music, or a theme that is repeated in a work of literature.

words.ex: The old house remained unaltered for 100 years.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子100年来一直未被改变。
words.en: If something is unaltered, it has stayed the same and has not been changed in any way.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.ex: The unemployment rate is an economic indicator.
words.ex_cn: 失业率是一个经济指标。
words.en: An indicator is a measurement or value which gives you an idea of what something is like.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: The movie is controversial because it shows violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因为展示暴力而有争议。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

words.ex: The handwriting is legible and easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 字迹清晰，容易辨认。
words.en: If writing or print is legible, it is clear enough to read.

words.ex: This rule applies to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: He tried to decipher the secret code.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破译那个秘密代码。
words.en: To decipher something means to convert it from a code into normal language or to understand something that is difficult to understand or that is not obvious.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.tr: adj. 筋疲力尽的；耗尽的； v. 耗尽；用完；“exhaust”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was exhausted after running five kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 他跑完五公里后筋疲力尽。
words.en: If you are exhausted, you are very tired and have no energy left.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.ex: He envelops the gift in colorful paper.
words.ex_cn: 他用彩色纸把礼物包起来。
words.en: To wrap up, cover, or surround completely.

words.ex: I occasionally walk my dog in the park.
words.ex_cn: 我偶尔在公园遛狗。
words.en: If something happens occasionally, it happens sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: The mirror deflects the light to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 镜子把光线反射到墙上。
words.en: If you deflect something such as criticism or attention, you act in a way that prevents it from being directed towards you or affecting you.

words.ex: This is the optimal time to plant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这是种植花卉的最佳时间。
words.en: Most favorable or desirable; best.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.tr: v. 提供；供应；“provide”的过去式和过去分词； conj. 如果；假如；在…条件下；
words.ex: The school provides free lunch to students.
words.ex_cn: 学校为学生提供免费午餐。
words.en: If a particular condition is true or if a particular event happens, then another condition will be true or another event will happen.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.tr: phrase. 回顾起来；事后看来；回想当初
words.ex: In retrospect, I should have studied harder.
words.ex_cn: 回想起来，我本该更努力学习的。
words.en: When you consider something in retrospect, you think about it afterwards, and often have a different opinion about it from the one that you had at the time.

words.tr:
n. 金额；总数；
v. 概括；
words.ex: The sum of the bill is fifty dollars.
words.ex_cn: 账单的金额是五十美元。
words.en: A sum is an amount of money, or the total amount of two or more amounts of money added together.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；讨厌的；
words.ex: The noisy neighbors are troublesome.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的邻居令人烦恼。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as troublesome, you mean that they cause you a lot of problems or worries.

words.ex: He likes reading books; moreover, he writes his own stories.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读书；此外，他还写自己的故事。
words.en: You use moreover to introduce a piece of information that adds to or supports the previous statement.

words.ex: His quest for truth led him to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他对真理的探求使他环游世界。
words.en: A quest is a long or difficult search for something.

words.ex: The fish spawn in the river each spring.
words.ex_cn: 鱼每年春天在河里产卵。
words.en: To spawn means to produce or deposit eggs, especially in large quantities, as fish, frogs, etc. do. It can also mean to give rise to or generate something.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.tr: adj. 不加选择的；不加区别的；
words.ex: The bombing was indiscriminate and hurt many civilians.
words.ex_cn: 这次轰炸是不加选择的，伤害了许多平民。
words.en: If you describe an action as indiscriminate, you are critical of it because it does not involve any careful thought or choice.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.tr: n. 仔细研究；详细检查；
words.ex: The teacher examined the student's work under close scrutiny.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了仔细研究。
words.en: If someone or something is under scrutiny, they are being studied or observed very carefully.

words.ex: Henceforth, I will wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 从今以后，我会早起。
words.en: From this time on; from now on.

words.ex: The apple will rot if left in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 如果把苹果放在太阳下，它会腐烂。
words.en: If something rots, or if it is left to rot, it decays and falls apart because of natural processes. Rot can also refer to a state of decay or decomposition.

words.ex: The wheel rotates slowly.
words.ex_cn: 轮子缓慢地转动。
words.en: To rotate means to turn or cause to turn around an axis or center.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.ex: The manifestation of his anger was a loud shout.
words.ex_cn: 他愤怒的显示是一声大喊。
words.en: A manifestation is an event, action, or object that clearly shows or embodies something, especially a theory or an abstract idea.

words.tr: n. 服饰；马饰；装饰；外部标志
words.ex: He wore the trappings of a judge during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿上了法官的服饰。
words.en: The trappings of a particular role or job are the extra things, such as titles and ceremonies, that go with it but are not necessary to it.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: This house has a modern design.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子具有现代的设计。
words.en: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

words.ex: He listens to classical music every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上听古典音乐。
words.en: Classical refers to music, literature, or art that is considered to be of the highest quality and of lasting value, especially from the ancient Greek or Roman periods or from the 18th and early 19th centuries.

words.tr: adj. 感伤的；感情的；多愁善感的
words.ex: He kept the old toy because he was sentimental about it.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了那个旧玩具，因为他对它有感情。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sentimental, you mean that they are influenced by emotional feelings, especially about happy memories of past events or relationships with other people, rather than by careful thought and judgment based on facts.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.ex: Plankton float in the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 浮游生物漂浮在海洋中。
words.en: Plankton are the diverse collection of organisms found in water (or air) that are unable to propel themselves against a current (or wind).

words.ex: Needless to say, he was late again.
words.ex_cn: 不用说，他又迟到了。
words.en: used to say that something is so obvious that it does not need to be mentioned

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.tr:
prep. 除…以外；
adv. 此外；
words.ex: Besides apples, he likes oranges.
words.ex_cn: 除了苹果，他还喜欢橙子。
words.en: In addition to; apart from.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: This is a good instance of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An instance is a particular example or case of something.

words.ex: She adorned her room with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用鲜花装饰了房间。
words.en: To adorn something means to make it more beautiful by adding something to it.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: The baby ingests milk every few hours.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿每隔几小时喝奶。
words.en: To ingest means to take food, drink, or another substance into your body, usually by swallowing.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.
